strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly articulates why existing KV cache quantization methods fail for long-CoT LLMs due to cumulative error and short-context calibration limitations
Strong and comprehensive experiments: Evaluates 7B-70B models on multiple benchmarks (AIME, CMIMC, LiveCode, IFEval) with consistent 8% improvements and 2.73-5.18× throughput gains

Novel technical combination: While individual components exist, the integration of progressive quantization, block-wise allocation, and positional interpolation is well-motivated for long-CoT scenarios
Elegant mathematical contributions: Equivalent Right Shift strategy (Eq. 3) is clever with formal proof; Integer Programming formulation for block allocation is principled
Thorough ablation studies: Tables 4-5 and Figures 3-4 validate each component; particularly convincing on bit-width shrinking strategies comparison
Impressive performance at extreme quantization: Achieves 64.79% vs 51.88% (KIVI) on 70B model at 2-bit, where baselines fail completely
Reproducibility: Public datasets, code promised, detailed experimental setup, extensive appendices with implementation details
weaknesses: Limited individual technical novelty: Progressive quantization is intuitive but straightforward; block-wise allocation and positional interpolation adapt existing techniques; main contribution is their combination

Throughput overhead underexplored: Table 3 shows 16% slowdown vs KIVI (424.72 vs 506.72 tokens/s) but paper claims overhead is negligible without detailed analysis of causes or potential optimizations

Positional interpolation lacks rigor: Scaling factor s fixed at 4 with limited exploration (Table 5); no principled guidance for choosing s; connection between s=4 (8K length) and actual 54K-token channel period undefined

Progressive quantization benefits not quantified: Missing empirical analysis of cumulative error reduction; Table 12 shows variable response lengths but lacks breakdown of when progressive quantization helps vs uniform Fbit

Evaluation scope limitations: Only DeepSeek-R1-Distill and QwQ tested; MLA attention mechanism explicitly excluded but increasingly important; KVTuner comparison limited to one model; fake quantization vs real INT kernels
Integer Programming overhead: Pre-inference costs 22.5-23.5% (Table 11); bit-width set B restricted to {2,4} or {4,8}; no guidance for choosing B for new models
Block sensitivity analysis incomplete: Figures 3-4 show variation across models (Qwen vs LLaMA) but no explanation of causes or prediction for new models
Comparison fairness: Different batch sizes for different methods and different GPUs make throughput comparisons less direct; baselines completely fail at 2-bit limiting informativeness
